IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript:
We regularly inspect trees near overhead power lines to keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. A recent inspection found some trees have grown too close to power lines. If unmanaged, branches could touch the overhead lines and cause unexpected interruptions to your electricity supply. We need to trim these trees, which requires a temporary power cut because the work cannot be done safely while electricity lines are live. Whilst the power is off our engineers will also be carrying out a repair on our electricity network. The work involves approximately 400 metres of tree cutting across 5 sections of the overhead network.
 There will be brief interruptions to your power while it is connected and removed. We appreciate your area has been impacted with unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. This work is taking place along the A20 Main Road. Please note there will be a lane closure on the A20 Main Road and multi way traffic lights on Farningham roundabout between 0930-1530 on both days.

MainMessage: We are aware of an incident caused by LV Fuse Replacement/Linking affecting the electricity supply in your area. Steps.Message:
Sent by Kevin at 06:30 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is on our overhead network affecting 381 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 08:30 and 09:30. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.
